knowledge_point.title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,\frac{3\pi }{4}\le 2x+y\le \pi ,\,0\le y+z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV={\int }_{3\pi /4}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,\frac{3\pi }{4}\le u\le \pi ,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2(1-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{1}{2}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /4}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,\pi \le x+y\le 2\pi ,\,0\le y+z\le \pi ,\,0\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$ 

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps: 

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,\pi \le u\le 2\pi ,\,0\le v\le \pi ,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

  

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |1|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le \frac{2x-y}{2}\le 1,\,0\le \frac{y}{2}\le 2,\,0\le z\le 3\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3},
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3},
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=6.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}(u+w)\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}(u+w)\cdot |6|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,6(u+w)\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le {x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\le 2,\,2\le x+y\le 4,\,0\le z\le 1\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables

$$
u={x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,v=x+y,\,w=z,
$$

the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+y)\operatorname{sinh}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dV
$$

can be written in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w$ as
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$ 

Note that the change of variables

$$
u={x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,v=x+y,\,w=z,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps: 

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,2\le v\le 4,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2x & -2y & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}2x & -2y \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2x+2y \\  & =2(x+y) \\  & =2v\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2v}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$ 

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+y)\operatorname{sinh}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}v\operatorname{sinh}⁡u\cdot |\frac{1}{2v}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡u}{2}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡u}{2}\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$
